articles.title: How Democrats expanded the map and won rural America
articles.summary: The victories followed a years-long Democratic effort to compete more aggressively in rural communities, where the party had steadily ceded ground to Republicans

items: A Democratic fundraiser in Iowa in October 2025 highlighted growing enthusiasm for the party in rural America, traditionally a Republican stronghold, which contributed to significant Democratic victories in the midterm elections a year later.

Democrats successfully flipped seats in rural areas by investing in local campaigns and engaging with voters, particularly focusing on issues affecting farmers and Hispanic communities disillusioned with Trump's policies.

To maintain their gains, Democrats must continue their expansive electoral strategy and outreach efforts in rural communities, as historical trends show that midterm successes do not guarantee presidential victories.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
A Democratic Party fundraiser in Warren County, Iowa, in October 2025 was so crowded that local party chair Jim Culbert found himself ordering pizza after the food ran out.
“If we don’t have enough food, that’s a good problem,” he recalled telling volunteers.

The big turnout offered an early glimpse of the mounting Democratic enthusiasm in rural America — traditionally a stronghold of US President Donald Trump‘s Republican party. A year later, it would help propel Democrats to sweeping victories in Tuesday’s midterm elections.

Democrats flipped House, Senate and gubernatorial seats in rural Republican strongholds including in Iowa, Kansas, Texas and Wisconsin, where farmers have been hard hit by Trump’s global tariff campaign and high fuel prices caused by the Iran war. Hispanic voters, who surveys identified as particularly critical of Trump’s deportation campaign and the rising cost of living, swung roughly 40 points towards Democrats in the Kansas and Texas Senate races compared to the 2024 presidential election, according to exit polls.

blocks.caption: Democrats flex congressional majorities as Trump accepts electoral losses

blocks.text: The victories followed a years-long Democratic effort to compete more aggressively in rural communities, where the party had steadily ceded ground to Republicans, according to interviews with 16 Democratic candidates, campaign staff and political experts and strategists.

Democratic strategists said that push was part of a broader Democratic National Committee effort to compete in places the party had long neglected. Rather than concentrating resources on a handful of battleground states, the DNC invested in every state party and pushed to field candidates in every race, they said.

“A lot of folks in rural America feel left behind because (Democrats) haven’t been showing up to talk to people,” said Democrat Rebecca Cooke, who unseated the Republican incumbent to win Wisconsin’s third congressional district on Tuesday. Now, she told Reuters, “there’s no community too small” to visit.

The question now is whether Democrats can hold on to their gains through the 2028 presidential election cycle. Tuesday’s election was widely seen as a rebuke of Trump rather than an embrace of the Democratic Party.

Republicans still won races on Tuesday in rural states including Arkansas, Oklahoma and Nebraska. And history shows that so-called wave elections dominated by one party do not necessarily translate into a presidential victory for the same party two years later.

To make their gains durable, Democrats will need to stick with their expansive electoral strategy, continuing to invest time and money in rural communities and other areas where they have made inroads, three Democratic strategists told Reuters.

“This was a rejection in essence of the way the party had worked in recent years, which was this focus on six or seven states,” said Simon Rosenberg, a Democratic strategist. “We had been operating on a very narrow map — too narrow.”
Rural Americans have steadily moved towards the Republican party over the past 25 years, according to Pew Research Center, driven by splits with Democrats on cultural issues and economic policies.
At the White House, Trump acknowledged that the Iran war had contributed to his party’s midterm losses but said he still felt it was worth it.
The Republican National Committee did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Every week for 11 months, on what she dubbed “Small Town Tuesday,” Iowa Democratic House candidate Christina Bohannan, focused on canvassing rural towns. Her team regularly heard from residents that no political campaign had ever contacted them before, campaign manager Dan Driscoll said in an email. Bohannan flipped the state’s first congressional district.
For her campaign in Wisconsin, Cooke said she hired four regional field organizers and knocked on 54,000 doors, many in rural areas, in addition to those knocked on by the statewide Democratic Party.
The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee said it implemented a program for engaging rural voters for the first time this year.

Cooke, Bohannan and other Democratic candidates in rural districts aimed to capitalize on declining support for Trump. Approval of the president in rural areas fell to a new low in October of 45%, down from 60% at the start of his term, according to Reuters/Ipsos polling.

Across more than 1,500 rural counties where nearly all ballots had been counted on Wednesday, Republican candidates were collectively underperforming Trump’s 2024 share of the vote by 8 percentage points, according vote totals compiled by Reuters and USA Today, which are partnering this year to collect live election results for US Senate and House races.

In Iowa, Democratic candidates united for the state’s first coordinated campaign since 2018, said Frances Patano, who ran the effort for the Iowa Democratic Party. That meant candidates could chip into a joint organizing effort that saved on costs and boosted lower-profile campaigns.
“By coordinating, you can run a far more efficient field program because you’re not competing” for the same group of organizers, Patano said.
In the first two weekends of October, the statewide campaign nearly doubled its door knock attempts from the 2018 midterms, Patano said.
In rural Warren County, the coordinated program paid for a staffer who led six canvassing shifts every weekend out of the county’s party office.

The added capacity boosted volunteer turnout. After years of organizing the same local Democrats to volunteer, Culbert said he would glance at a list of doorknockers and think: “Well, I don’t know half these names.”
In Kansas, efforts to elect Adam Hamilton, the first Democratic senator elected from the state in nearly a century, began four years ago.

When Jeanna Repass became chair of the Kansas Democratic Party in 2022, she knew the party would need to make inroads in a heavily rural state that Trump won by double digits in 2016 and 2020. She hired a year-round organizer and grew the number of county party chapters from 57 to 68.
The effort “helped us to stir people’s passions and get them organized,” Repass said.

This year, the party knocked about 50% more doors than they did in the 2022 midterms, Repass said. That strategy paid dividends for Hamilton on Tuesday, particularly in Seward County, where about half of eligible voters are Hispanic.
Hamilton won by 13 points in Seward, a dramatic shift from 2024 when Trump won the county by 39 points.
“We are not flyover country,” Hamilton said in his victory speech late on Tuesday night, to huge cheers. “We are the heart of America.” – Rappler.com

Prominent Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong was sentenced to 10 years in prison Thursday for his second conviction under a Beijing-imposed national security law, in a case that critics say reflects the crackdown on the city's once-thriving pro-democracy movement.
Wong is already serving a near 5-year prison term for his part in the city's biggest national security case

Wong was charged in 2025 with conspiracy to collude with foreign forces to endanger national security under the law. In September he pleaded guilty to the offence, a move that can typically reduce the sentence.

The 30-year-old is already serving a four-year, eight-month prison term for the city's biggest national security case after entering a guilty plea. Before being prosecuted for the collusion-related charge, Wong had been expected to be freed in January 2027.

Judge William Tam said during the sentencing hearing that Wong's offence was of a grave nature and rejected that his role was limited. He also said he considered a 13-year prison sentence as a starting point but reduced it because of Wong's guilty plea.
Wong looked calm and thanked his supporters before leaving the court. His supporters waved to him and Tiffany Chin, a former member of the now-disbanded Scholarism, once led by Wong, was in tears.
The judge said Wong could serve his two prison sentences concurrently. Wong only has about two months left on the sentence for his previous national security conviction.
Supporters attend court

Some members of the public started queuing outside the court building as early as Tuesday to secure a seat in the public gallery. Activist Lui Yuk-lin held a piece of paper carrying Wong's name in the line Thursday.

Resident ET Wong said that when Joshua Wong was just teenager, he possessed "big-picture thinking" that some adults might not even have. He walked a difficult path for Hong Kong's future, human rights and student movement, she said.
"At least in my heart, he should not have spent a single day in wrongful imprisonment," she said.
People line up outside Hong Kong's High Court ahead of a Thursday morning sentencing. (Tyrone Siu/Reuters)
Chilling dissent

Hong Kong once had a freewheeling civil society marked by its vibrant protest and media scenes. But after an anti-government movement rocked the city in 2019, authorities reduced public choice in elections and arrested many leading activists. Some news outlets known for their reports critical of the government shut down and dozens of civil society groups dissolved.
Observers say Wong's sentencing shows the authorities' determination to keep prominent activists in prison for as long as possible, further chilling civic activism.

"NSL charges can be repeatedly weaponized to keep a specific political prisoner in jail, if the government deems necessary," said Eric Lai, a research fellow at Georgetown Center for Asian Law, referring to the national security law.

items: Hong Kong's new security law expands scope abroad. What to know about the Article 23 laws
Hong Kong activist Agnes Chow still fears Beijing's reach despite living in Canada

blocks.text: But Beijing views Wong as an anti-China figure supporting Hong Kong independence, a stance that crosses its red line. Hong Kong authorities also said the security law is crucial for the city's stability following the 2019 protests, maintaining that the city's law enforcement actions were evidence-based.

Wong, second from left, with activists Eddie Chu, Owen Chow and Lester Shum, posing with signs in support of the 12 Hong Kong activists held in mainland China after attempting to flee the city for Taiwan, in Hong Kong, October 20, 2020. (Lam Yik/Reuters)
Prosecution focused on Wong's lobbying and advocacy

The prosecution previously alleged that Wong and fellow activist Nathan Law had agreed in or around 2016 to lobby internationally to achieve their goal of democratic self-determination. It said that before the security law was introduced, the pair had been calling for sanctions and other adverse measures against Hong Kong and China. It pointed to his meetings with U.S. politicians like Nancy Pelosi and Marco Rubio in 2016 and 2019.

After the law was enacted, Law and others advanced their work abroad by meeting foreign politicians and launching petition drives, it said. Wong supported the effort from Hong Kong through foreign media outlets and social media to draw foreign countries' attention and bolster the request for sanctions, blockade or other hostile measures against China and Hong Kong, it said.
His lawyer Derek Chan earlier urged the court to impose a sentence that would give his client some hope, adding that Wong wishes to take care of his parents after his release.
China hasn't 'imprisoned his spirit': Jimmy Lai's son on father's sentencing
His friends said during his nearly six years in prison, Wong has kept reading books and exercising, teaching himself guitar while maturing in his thinking.
To his supporters, Wong is a political star representing a younger generation born in the final years of Hong Kong's British colonial rule before the city's return to China in 1997.
Despite being held behind bars, Wong's influence appears to have remained a concern, at least for the pro-Beijing camp.

In September, a pro-Beijing newspaper report criticized a 2017 documentary about Wong on Netflix for "beautifying" his crimes. The city's security bureau told local media the government was taking follow-up action.
But the documentary then shot to the top of Netflix's popular chart in Hong Kong.

articles.title: Valkyries celebrate WNBA championship with San Francisco and Oakland fans
articles.summary: Dancing in the streets, popping champagne and high-fiving fans was all part of the celebration on Wednesday as the Golden State Valkyries parade made its way through Oakland and then across the bay…

image.caption: Golden State Valkyries' Kaitlyn Chen sprays champagne toward fans during the team's WNBA championship parade in San Francisco Wednesday. (Stephen Lam/San Francisco Chronicle/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·Photos

Dancing in the streets, popping champagne and high-fiving fans was all part of the celebration on Wednesday as the Golden State Valkyries parade made its way through Oakland and then across the bay in San Francisco.
The team honoured fans on both sides of the bay as they celebrated their victory Wednesday
The newest WNBA champs encouraged their California fans to call in sick, skip out on work or ditch school Wednesday — and elated basketball fans appeared thrilled to take their advice.
Tens of thousands of people lined the streets for a Golden State Valkyries victory parade after the team sealed the championship on Saturday in a 68-63 Game 7 win over the Atlanta Dream.

There was dancing, champagne, team colours and plenty of high-fives. And of course, team mascot Vi. She's a raven, commonly seen as a sidekick to Valkyries in Norse mythology, according to the team website.
Golden State Valkyries mascot Violet, also known as Vi, rides on a float during the team's WNBA championship parade. (Darren Yamashita/Imagn Images/Reuters)
Oakland to San Francisco

The Valkyries began their day of celebration at Oakland's Jack London Square, not far from the team's downtown practice facility, then took a ferry across the bay to begin the parade from San Francisco's Ferry Building.
It concluded near the San Francisco Giants' Oracle Park.
Golden State Valkyries centre Kiah Stokes at the parade kickoff rally at Jack London Square in Oakland, Calif. (Yalonda M. James/San Francisco Chronicle/The Asscociated Press)
The players posed for photos onstage with the WNBA championship trophy at Jack London Square in Oakland before hopping on a ferry across San Francisco Bay. (Darren Yamashita/Imagn Images/Reuters)
Valkyries forward Kayla Thornton. (Darren Yamashita/Imagn Images/Reuters)
Year 2 championship
Golden State was granted an expansion franchise three years ago. At the time, team owner Joe Lacob guaranteed a championship within five years.

His promise was honoured as the team led by coach Natalie Nakase delivered an improbable title in Year 2 after becoming the first expansion franchise to reach the playoffs in its inaugural year in 2025.
Fans turned out for the parade in the team's colours from head to toe. (Darren Yamashita/Imagn Images/Reuters)
Valkyries fans cheered from a rooftop as the parade rolled past. (Darren Yamashita/Imagn Images/Reuters)
'Too small' goes big
After the Dream beat the Valkyries in Game 3, Atlanta player Angel Reese taunted the Valkyries' bench with a hand gesture for "too small."
But some Valkyries turned the taunt into a power move after their victory, and brought it out for the parade.
Valkyries guard Juste Jocyte gives the 'too small' gesture, started by Angel Reese in Game 3, to the fans during the Valkyries parade. (David Gonzales/Imagn Images/Reuters)
Valkyries guard Tiffany Hayes celebrated from the double decker bus as it made its way through San Francisco. (Darren Yamashita/Imagn Images/Reuters)

articles.title: Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 years in prison in national security case
articles.summary:
Wong, 30, has been imprisoned since 2020 and is the only activist in Hong Kong prosecuted twice under national security law

Hong Kong activist

blocks.text: Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong was sentenced on Thursday to 10 years in prison after pleading guilty to “foreign collusion”, his second conviction under a national security law that critics say has been used to silence political opposition in the city.

Wong, who rose to prominence as the teenage face of Hong Kong’s 2014 pro-democracy demonstrations, submitted his plea in September. He had been accused of working with the exiled Hong Kong activist Nathan Law to urge foreign powers to impose sanctions, blockades or other hostile measures against China.
In his ruling, High ​court Judge William Tam ‌described Wong’s actions as “grave in nature”.

He said Wong had visited the US to seek foreign interference ahead of the national security law’s introduction in 2020, and continued to share posts on social media by Law calling for sanctions after it was enacted.
Wong’s role was to “supply his underground support” and “arouse the attention of foreign countries to bolster the cause” of exiled activists, the judge said.
He said Wong’s sentence will run concurrently with the remaining term of his previous national security offence.
Wong wore a dark blue shirt and thick rimmed glasses in court, and nodded and bowed as supporters waved.

The former student leader is already serving a prison term of four years and eight months, imposed in November 2024, for conspiracy to commit subversion for his role in an unofficial primary election. He has spent nearly six years in detention and had been due to be released in January 2027.

Wong, 30, gained international attention during the 2014 Umbrella protests, which paralysed the city’s financial centre and galvanised a generation of young people. In October 2014, he appeared – with his trademark black-rimmed spectacles – on the cover of a Time magazine under the headline: “The Face of Protest”.

When protests erupted in 2019 over a proposed extradition bill, Wong was serving a prison sentence for his role in the 2014 demonstrations. He was released at the height of the protests and immediately took to the streets.

The following year, Beijing introduced a sweeping national security law it said was needed to restore stability to the former British colony, but critics say has been used to target political opposition, dissolve civil society groups and silence independent media.

articles.title: El Niño now very strong, impacts to be felt until 2027
articles.summary: PAGASA projections show the very strong El Niño or so-called Super El Niño may cause drought in virtually the entire country by March 2027

blocks.text: MONITORING. The Manila City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Department monitors the El Niño phenomenon, October 15, 2026.
Rappler
PAGASA projections show the very strong El Niño or so-called Super El Niño may cause drought in virtually the entire country by March 2027

items: The 2026-2027 El Niño in the tropical Pacific Ocean is now considered very strong.
The Philippines is among the countries facing the severe impacts of El Niño, with the agriculture sector badly hit.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – A very strong El Niño is now present in the tropical Pacific Ocean, the Philippine weather bureau announced in a statement posted on Thursday, November 5.
Also informally called Super El Niño, this current episode of the weather phenomenon might reach its peak by the end of 2026, but persist until the first half of 2027.
In the Philippines, El Niño leads to less rainfall, causing dry spells and drought.

The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) defines a dry spell as three straight months of below normal rainfall or two straight months of way below normal rainfall.
Drought, meanwhile, is experienced when there is three straight months of way below normal rainfall or five straight months of below normal rainfall.
Below normal refers to a 21% to 60% drop from the average rainfall volume in a particular area, while way below normal means a reduction of more than 60%.

PAGASA expects below normal to way below normal rainfall in most parts of the country in November. Temperatures are also likely to be higher than average, despite the presence of the northeast monsoon or amihan, which brings cool air.
By the end of November, the following areas may have drought, according to PAGASA forecasts:

items: Luzon – Albay, Camarines Norte, Camarines Sur, Catanduanes
Visayas – Capiz, Leyte, Negros Oriental, Samar, Siquijor, Southern Leyte
Mindanao – Isabela City, Misamis Oriental

blocks.text: These areas could be experiencing dry spells by the end of the month:

items: Luzon – Abra, Apayao, Bataan, Batanes, Batangas, Benguet, Cagayan, Cavite, Ifugao, Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, Isabela, Palawan (Kalayaan), Kalinga, La Union, Marinduque, Masbate, Mountain Province, Metro Manila, Nueva Vizcaya, Occidental Mindoro, Oriental Mindoro, Palawan, Pangasinan, Quezon, Quirino, Romblon, Sorsogon, Zambales
Visayas – Aklan, Antique, Biliran, Bohol, Cebu, Guimaras, Iloilo, Negros Occidental, Northern Samar

Mindanao – Basilan, Camiguin, Cotabato, Davao del Sur, Davao Occidental, Dinagat Islands, Maguindanao del Norte, Maguindanao del Sur, Misamis Occidental, Sarangani, South Cotabato, Special Geographic Area, Sultan Kudarat, Sulu, Surigao del Norte, Tawi-Tawi, Zamboanga del Norte, Zamboanga del Sur, Zamboanga Sibugay

blocks.text: By March 2027, virtually the entire country may face drought, further affecting agriculture, water resources, energy, and public health.

“The public and all concerned agencies are strongly advised to implement appropriate sectoral interventions, conservation and mitigation measures, particularly water conservation and efficient management of water resources, to minimize the potential impacts of El Niño,” PAGASA Administrator Nathaniel Servando said in a statement.

blocks.caption: What schools will do amid intense heat during El Niño

blocks.text: El Niño has already caused massive damage and losses to agriculture this year. As of October 21, the Department of Agriculture (DA) pegged the cost of damage at P8.57 billion, with more than 288,000 farmers affected.

The DA said its assistance so far includes P10.81 billion worth of production support, such as seeds, fertilizers, and soil conditioner, as well as P569.95 million worth of Philippine Crop Insurance Corporation indemnification for 68,980 affected farmers.
In a worst-case scenario, according to the DA, the Super El Niño could affect around 4.6 million of the country’s 10.4 million farmers and fisherfolk.

blocks.caption: [OPINION] From Super El Niño to the budget: What is the plan?

blocks.text: El Niño is the warm phase of El Niño Southern Oscillation or ENSO, which the World Meteorological Organization defines as “a recurring natural phenomenon characterized by fluctuating ocean temperatures in the equatorial Pacific, coupled with changes in the atmosphere.” ENSO has two other phases: La Niña or the cool phase, and neutral.

El Niño does not mean complete absence of rainfall in the Philippines. Weather systems such as tropical cyclones, the northeast monsoon, the intertropical convergence zone, and the easterlies can still trigger rain in the coming months.
PAGASA said two to six tropical cyclones may develop within or enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility from November 2026 to April 2027. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Mon Tulfo admits mistake in Romualdez report: 'I was fed the wrong report'
articles.summary: Columnist Ramon Tulfo apologized on Thursday for reporting that Leyte Representative and former House Speaker Martin Romualdez had snuck out of prison, saying he was given the wrong information.

blocks.text: Published November 5, 2026 11:17am
Columnist Ramon Tulfo apologized on Thursday for reporting that Leyte Representative and former House Speaker Martin Romualdez had snuck out of prison, saying he was given the wrong information.
In a Facebook post, Tulfo said it was “embarrassing and humiliating” to admit that he was fed the wrong information and accepted it as gospel truth.
He added worse was he passed it on to his readers who "trust me and took me on my word."
“I was fed the wrong report that former speaker Martin Romualdez could go in and out of jail,” he said.

“Complete with all the details like riding in an ambulance and the brownouts taking place so he would not be seen going out and coming back in,” he added. “No such thing happened when the facts started coming in yesterday.”
On Tuesday, Tulfo posted information from a source he referred to as his “tweety bird.”

He claimed that Quezon City Jail-Male Dormitory Superintendent Maria Lourdes Pacion allegedly switches off the facility's electricity whenever Romualdez leaves and returns, to prevent CCTV footage from being recorded.
This prompted the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology to launch an investigation into the claims.
The Sandiganbayan Third Division also ordered officials of the BJMP to testify on Thursday regarding the status of Romualdez in detention.
Tulfo said there’s no excuse for his blunder.
“I goofed. No excuses. I should have first checked and cross-checked that report I received on Romualdez,” he said. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Ex-law dean withdraws as defense witness in Sara Duterte impeachment trial
articles.summary: A former law school dean who was invited by the team of Vice President Sara Duterte has declined to testify for the defense.

blocks.text: November 5, 2026 | 10:59am
The Senate impeachment court votes on the threshold required to convict an impeachable official on Sept. 23, 2026, with 13 senator-judges voting in favor and one against.
Senate of the Philippines / Joseph Vidal via Facebook
MANILA, Philippines — A former law school dean who was invited by the team of Vice President Sara Duterte has declined to testify for the defense.

In a statement on Thursday, November 5, former University of St. La Salle College of Law dean Ralph Sarmiento said that he was declining the defense panel’s invitation to “preserve the independence” of his “constitutional law scholarship” and the impartiality of his legal views and opinions.
“I had not anticipated that these views might potentially become part of the impeachment proceedings,” Sarmiento said.
“After careful consideration, I have decided to decline participation as a witness in the proceedings,” he added.
Sarmiento said that he had already reached out to the defense team, asking it to withdraw its request for a subpoena or his appearance.
The former law school dean was supposed to be the first witness to be presented by the defense team.

In their manifestation, Duterte’s defense team said that Sarmiento was expected to provide testimony regarding legal and constitutional principles relevant to the case, with a specific focus on Article II of the Articles of Impeachment.

Article II accuses Duterte of culpable violation of the Constitution and betrayal of public trust over her alleged unexplained wealth, discrepancies in her Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALNs), and alleged failure to divest from business interests while serving as vice president.
Duterte’s defense team cited Sarmiento’s credentials as a professor of Political and Constitutional Law as evidence of his capacity as a witness.
The defense team’s spokesperson, Michael Poa, said that the panel respects his decision.
“We respect Dean Sarmiento’s personal decision and appreciate his initial consideration of our invitation,” Poa said.
“We wish him well in his continued contributions to constitutional discourse,” he added.
Other witnesses are also expected to be disclosed in subsequent filings for hearings scheduled for November 10, 11, 12, 13, 19, 20 and 23.

articles.title: BJMP: Romualdez has 'personal staff' while in detention; lawmaker never left jail
articles.summary: A personal staff of former Speaker and Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez is staying with the lawmaker in his cell in the New Quezon City jail, the jail warden of the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology…

blocks.text: Published November 5, 2026 10:58am

A personal staff of former Speaker and Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez is staying with the lawmaker in his cell in the New Quezon City jail, the jail warden of the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) on Thursday.

BJMP Jail Warden Lourdes Pacion made the testimony during the hearing on the status of Romualdez's detention amid allegations of columinist Ramon Tulfo that the former speaker is able to leave the BJMP facility as he pleases in an ambulance.
"He has personal staff to help him in his daily needs," Pacion said.
Asked by the anti-court if the personal staff of Romualdez stays with the lawmaker inside his cell, Pacion answered in the affirmative.
Mental state
Pacion said allowing a personal staff or an individual to look after a person deprived of liberty is allowed on a case-to-case basis.
"I allowed it because his mental state is not yet stable per my assessment. We cannot hire more personnel to attend to the personal needs of Congressman Romualdez," Pacion said.

"We are allowing personal staff to stay inside the jail for humanitarian consideration, or if the patient is not in good condition, because we cannot attend to all personal needs of the patient," Pacion added.
Tulfo on Thursday morning, meanwhile, clarified that his information of Romualdez leaving detention facility is "false."
“I was fed the wrong report that former speaker Martin Romualdez could go in and out of jail,” Tulfo said.
Ahead of Tulfo's clarification, Pacion told the anti-graft court that Romualdez never left the BJMP premises in ambulance or any other vehicle.

"We categorically deny that information, your honor. Since the commitment of Congressman Romualdez [in detention], he stays in his room (cell). Once in a while he goes in the sunny area [of the detention facility]. For court hearings, he goes to the court room [provided by the facility]," Pacion said
"He did not go out riding an ambulance or any other vehicle," Pacion added.
Given Tulfo's retraction, the defense team of Romualdez put on record that Tulfo's previous allegation was untruthful and detrimental to their client.
"That was very damaging to our client because it has the tendency to inflame the public," the Romualdez's defense team said. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: DOF endorses $20-M UAE grant for Pasig River rehab to OP
articles.summary: The Department of Finance (DOF) said Thursday it endorsed a proposed $20-million, or approximately P1.2 billion, grant from the government of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to the Office of the…

blocks.text: Published November 5, 2026 10:50am

The Department of Finance (DOF) said Thursday it endorsed a proposed $20-million, or approximately P1.2 billion, grant from the government of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to the Office of the President (OP) for the rehabilitation of the Pasig River.

In a statement, the DOF said the proposed grant will support the Pasig River Restoration Project (PRRP), which targets a 25% reduction in plastic and organic waste entering the Pasig River system over five years.
Unlike loans, grants are forms of development assistance that do not require repayment.

Moreover, the Finance Department said the proposed grant underscores the Philippines' continued efforts to mobilize international partnerships and development assistance for environmental rehabilitation initiatives.

“We thank the Government of the United Arab Emirates for extending its hand in partnership with us to rehabilitate one of our country's vital waterways. The proposed assistance would strengthen waste management efforts and help improve the quality of life of our people,” said Finance Secretary Frederick Go.

The DOF said the project would cover five key areas of intervention, namely waste recovery and interception; household waste segregation and collection; capacity-building and support for informal waste collectors; improved waste processing and recovery; and stronger enforcement against illegal dumping.
The Finance Department said it is seeking the necessary authority to negotiate the proposed agreement, including its terms and conditions.
Once authorized, the DOF said it will facilitate negotiations with the UAE government in coordination with concerned government agencies. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Why Ralph Sarmiento refused to testify at Sara Duterte’s trial
articles.summary: The defense team had wanted the constitutional expert and former law dean to be their first witness in the Vice President's impeachment trial

blocks.text: RALPH SARMIENTO. The defense counsel of Vice President Sara Duterte had wanted law dean Ralph Sarmiento as their first witness but he declined.
The defense team had wanted the constitutional expert and former law dean to be their first witness in the Vice President's impeachment trial
MANILA, Philippines – The defense team of Vice President Sara Duterte will have to find another first witness for her impeachment trial which resumes on Monday, November 9.

In a video message on Thursday, November 5, former law school dean Ralph Sarmiento said he had declined the defense team’s request for him to testify, saying he wanted to preserve the independence of his constitutional law scholarship and the impartiality of his legal views.

This came a day after the defense identified Sarmiento as its first witness, submitting a manifestation before the Senate impeachment court seeking the issuance of subpoenas ad testificandum (or a summon to appear before the court) and duces tecum (to compel him to bring relevant documents including a copy of his curriculum vitae).
“After careful consideration, I have decided to decline participation as a witness in the proceedings,” said Sarmiento.
“This is a personal decision to preserve the independence of my constitutional law scholarship and the impartiality of my legal views and opinions,” he added.

The defense team had wanted the law professor to testify on legal and constitutional principles relevant to the impeachment case, particularly Article II, which involves Duterte’s alleged unexplained wealth.
He said he had already communicated with the defense to withdraw its request for a subpoena compelling his appearance, or seek its recall if it had already been issued.
“I remain committed to contributing to public understanding of the Constitution through independent and balanced legal analysis,” Sarmiento added.
Michael Poa, spokesperson for Duterte’s defense team, said they respected Sarmiento’s decision.
“We respect Dean Sarmiento’s personal decision and appreciate his initial consideration of our invitation. We wish him well in his continued contributions to constitutional discourse,” said Poa.
Sarmiento was law school dean of the University of St. La Salle in Bacolod City until September 30, 2025, and has since been the university’s vice chancellor for administration.
He earned his Juris Doctor degree in the University of St. La Salle. He was admitted to the Bar in 1997, placing 10th in the Bar exam.

A lawyer with expertise in International Law, Sarmiento also served as a bar lecturer and reviewer, and has authored several books including International Law: Compendium and Bar Reviewer and Bar Exam Logic: Mastering Legal Reasoning for the Bar Exams and Law Practice.

He had earlier called for fairness after the prosecution dropped three of four articles of impeachment against Duterte, saying the defense “should be given even just a limited opportunity to present rebuttal evidence in the same Impeachment Court, under oath and subject to cross-examination.”

The impeachment trial was temporarily paused to give way to the Senate committee hearings on the proposed 2027 national budget. The trial will resume on November 9, when the defense will begin its presentation of evidence. – Rappler.com

articles.summary: Tencent said it restricted the Hy4 AI model's cybersecurity training to defensive uses, such as identifying software flaws and helping fix them

blocks.text: TENCENT. The Tencent logo is seen in this illustration taken February 16, 2025.
Dado Ruvic/Reuters
Tencent said it restricted the Hy4 AI model's cybersecurity training to defensive uses, such as identifying software flaws and helping fix them

items: Tencent released Hy4, an AI model designed with limitations to prevent misuse in cyberattacks and harmful biological research.
The model's training focuses on defensive cybersecurity measures, excluding content related to hacking tools and system vulnerabilities.
Tencent emphasizes its commitment to responsible AI development and plans to release safety testing reports alongside the model weights.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

Chinese tech giant Tencent on Wednesday, November 4, released Hy4, a new AI model it said was designed with limits intended to reduce the risk that it could be used for cyberattacks or harmful biological research.

Tencent said it restricted the model’s cybersecurity training to defensive uses, such as identifying software flaws and helping fix them. It excluded material on building hacking tools, breaking into systems and testing systems for weaknesses.

The Shenzhen-based company and developer of WeChat, China’s most popular app with over ⁠1 billion monthly active users, said internal security specialists tested Hy4 and found no sign that it posed higher risks in helping users break into software or bypass security protections. Tencent also said its testing found that the model was not capable of meaningfully making harmful biological experiments easier to carry out.

The release comes at a time of surging global concern over AI-powered hacking and follows Tencent’s disclosure last month that AI agents it used to test third-party models displayed unintended web-browsing behavior. Researchers said agents linked to Tencent Cloud had sought information from Alibaba’s Amap service.

Tencent said the activity did not come from its Hunyuan models, and that its review found no evidence of deliberate targeting or coordination, while vowing to strengthen controls over agents’ internet access and monitoring.

Despite cutthroat domestic competition and an intensifying rivalry with the US, Chinese AI firms have in recent months shown signs of investing more in model safety. Beijing-based Moonshot AI last month limited its newest model’s cyber-offensive capabilities.
Tencent said it plans to release its model weights later along with a report describing its safety testing.

“We recognize the potential safety risks posed by advanced cyber and biological capabilities, and we are committed to a more responsible approach to model training, open-sourcing, and release,” Tencent said. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Alberta's governing UCP endorses proposed riding boundary changes as NDP reiterates concerns
articles.summary: Alberta's governing United Conservatives have officially endorsed changes to provincial riding boundaries that the Opposition NDP says it believes are “rigged” to help the UCP win the next election.

image.caption: A file photo of Alberta's provincial flag from July 2026. (Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Edmonton·New
Alberta's governing United Conservatives have officially endorsed changes to provincial riding boundaries that the Opposition NDP says it believes are “rigged” to help the UCP win the next election.
Justice minister defends rural-urban hybrid ridings, says such ridings already exist in Alberta
· The Canadian Press
· Posted: Nov 04, 2026 9:19 PM EST | Last Updated: 14 minutes ago
Premier Danielle Smith's UCP caucus, in a vote split along party lines, voted Wednesday to endorse the proposed riding changes and put the new boundaries into a bill to be debated in the house.
Justice Minister Mickey Amery has said he expects legislation to pass by the end of the year ahead of the scheduled election in October 2027.
The riding report came from a panel with a majority of members selected by the UCP.
The NDP alleges the report dilutes urban ridings in Lethbridge and Calgary by merging them with adjacent rural areas to favour the UCP in a process known as gerrymandering.

Gerrymandering, which is common in the United States, sees electoral districts drawn up not for reasons of shared geography and priorities but by voting patterns in order to assist one political party.

items: Province's last boundary panel chair urged new panellists not to alter southern Alberta ridings. They did.

blocks.text: Speaking during a debate of the proposals Wednesday, Amery defended the rural-urban hybrid ridings that have become the focus of debate, saying they already exist in Alberta.

"Hybrid ridings also do something else: they bring together communities that share services, employment, infrastructure and economic interests, regardless of whether a municipal boundary happens to run between them," said Amery.
With 2024 legislation, Smith's government removed the requirement that electoral boundaries respect municipal boundaries as a guiding principle.

The NDP has charged that the latest process to redraw the report was illegitimate from the start, and pleaded until the last minute for the UCP to instead revert to the map recommended by an independent public commission.
Nenshi said Wednesday that he believes the changes are designed to help vulnerable UCP ministers keep their seats.
"It strikes a knife into the heart of Alberta's democracy," he said.

items: New Alberta riding plan shifts thousands of Calgary, Lethbridge voters into rural-urban districts

blocks.text: The latest redrawing has been a controversial and complicated affair since the premier rejected the main recommendations of a public boundaries commission early this year. The commission came back with a split report.
Bucking political norms, Smith's government voted down the commission's majority position in the legislature and restarted the process with a new advisory panel.

Traditionally, Alberta's chief justice helps find a current or retired judge to chair and oversee the work. But earlier this year, the acting Alberta chief justice declined to participate, calling the new process "irregular."

The panel, chaired by retired Alberta justice Brian O'Ferrall, was given direction based on some recommendations from the previous commission's chair, including expanding the number of ridings to 91 from 87 to preserve two rural ridings that were to be dissolved.
Smith has said urban representation, amid population growth in cities, shouldn't come at the expense of rural Alberta.
But Nenshi told the house Wednesday the panel went well beyond those marching orders without justification and without considering public feedback.
Alberta panel proposes new electoral maps

The proposals would split the southern city of Lethbridge into four ridings from its current two. It would have one strictly urban riding while the other three would see some neighbourhoods linked to sprawling adjacent rural areas.
It also includes additional hybrid ridings for the west side of Calgary.
In question period earlier Wednesday, Smith called Nenshi's allegations "ridiculous," and said if anyone gerrymandered the maps to benefit the UCP, "they failed miserably."
She said under the proposed maps, if the UCP were to win the popular vote by the same margins as it did in the 2023 election, the NDP would gain three seats and the UCP would gain one.
"[Nenshi's] trying to set it up so that people will doubt the integrity of elections," she said.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Lisa Johnson
The Canadian Press
Lisa Johnson is a reporter for The Canadian Press based in Alberta.
With files from Jack Farrell

articles.title: Elon Musk’s nearly half a billion dollars in midterms spending was a flop
articles.summary:
The tech billionaire set spending record as he poured $446m into campaigns for failed Republican candidates

Elon Musk set a

blocks.text: Elon Musk set a record for election spending this year after pouring nearly half a billion dollars into backing Republicans in the US midterm elections. It turned out to be a poor investment.

The SpaceX and Tesla CEO contributed at least $446m to Republican-aligned Super Pacs and groups over the course of the elections, specifically targeting several key Senate races in an effort to help the Trump administration retain Republican control of Congress. He outdid his own 2024 spending of nearly $290m. Yet as Democrats swept to power across the country on Tuesday night, it became clear that Musk would get nearly nothing in return for his hundreds of millions in spending.

Democrats won every one of the five Senate races where Musk’s America Pac spent the most money backing Republican candidates. In Texas, where Musk’s empire is based and where he directed most of his political efforts, Republicans lost the Senate race, governor’s office and are expected to relinquish control of the state house.

After months of Musk posting attacks on Democrats and amplifying election conspiracy theories on X, the tech mogul was unusually quiet on election night. He jokingly posted “Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now,” but the top Republican mega-donor was otherwise largely silent on the results.

Musk’s losses from midterms go beyond the enormous sums that he dumped into failed campaigns, however, potentially ending an era of lax regulation and cozy relations with state officials that has benefitted his companies. The world’s richest person will soon face a House, Senate and Texas government filled with Democrats that have vowed to take a tougher stance on tech and specifically scrutinize his operations in particular.

Altogether, Musk’s political spending this midterms flowed into at least eight Republican-aligned Super Pacs that targeted races across the country, with the largest donation of at least $216m going into his own America Pac. He also gave $168m to the Senate Leadership Fund, which backed a series of candidates that included the Texas Republican Ken Paxton.

Out of all of Musk’s political activity in midterms, the contest where he put the most money and focus was the Senate race in Texas between Paxton and Democrat James Talarico. America Pac spent at least $28m on anti-Talarico ad buys and messaging alone, while Musk repeatedly posted attacks on X, his social media platform, such as “Talarico wants to trans your kids and destroy the border.”
After Talarico achieved a commanding win on Tuesday night, the Democratic senator-elect referenced Musk in his victory speech.
“We just proved that all the money in the world is no match for the people of Texas,” Talarico said. “We just sent a message to every billionaire mega-donor, every trillionaire mega-donor.”

Senate races in Michigan, Maine, Ohio and Iowa similarly went for Democratic candidates after America Pac spent tens of millions supporting Republican campaigns. The Pac’s money had gone into attack ads that focused on transgender rights or accused Democrats of being radical socialists.
after newsletter promotion

Even if Musk’s spending was not successful, it doesn’t mean it wasn’t impactful. Musk and the Super Pacs’ expenditures created several of the most expensive races in US history and set a potential precedent for how much spending will take place in the 2028 presidential election. It will also probably spur months of analysis around the limits of what money can buy in politics.

Musk’s businesses have benefitted greatly from lucrative contracts with the Trump administration, as well as Trump’s hands-off approach to regulating artificial intelligence. In Texas, the state legislature and Governor Greg Abbott have provided him a friendly environment to do business while passing laws backed by the billionaire’s lobbyists.

Gina Hinojosa, the incoming Democratic governor in Texas,will probably take a more critical stance towards Musk and his businesses. Hinojosa has called for a datacenter moratorium and has been in a legal battle in recent months to gain access to unredacted emails between Abbott’s office and Musk. Meanwhile, House Democrats have called for launching investigations into Musk’s conduct while he was leader of the so-called “department of government efficiency” last year and vowed to scrutinize federal funding for his companies.

articles.title: Motorcade honours B.C. soldier killed in fire at CFB Wainwright
articles.summary: Pte. Aidan Goulding from North Vancouverwas among four soldiers killed in the blaze that overwhelmed a live-fire training exercise at CFB Wainwright on Oct. 17.

image.caption: A hearse carrying the remains of Pte. Aidan Goulding leaves Vancouver International Airport under a police motorcade in Richmond, B.C., on Wednesday. Goulding, from North Vancouver, was among four soldiers killed in a fire at CFB Wainwright on Oct. 17. (Ethan Cairns/CBC)

blocks.text: British Columbia
Pte. Aidan Goulding from North Vancouverwas among four soldiers killed in the blaze that overwhelmed a live-fire training exercise at CFB Wainwright on Oct. 17.
Pte. Aidan Goulding from North Vancouver was one of 4 soldiers killed in Oct. 17 fire

The remains of a soldier killed in a grass fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta last month have returned to British Columbia, with dozens of police officers, firefighters and others gathering to pay their respects.
A motorcade escorted the hearse carrying Pte. Aidan Goulding's remains from the Vancouver airport to a funeral home in New Westminster on Wednesday.
Police and firefighters stood at attention and saluted as the hearse passed beneath a large Canadian flag strung over the road using fire truck ladders.
Emergency personnel and the public salute as the remains of Pte. Aidan Goulding pass underneath a Canadian flag. (Ethan Cairns/CBC)
Sgt. Maj. Ray Gardner from the Vancouver Police Department was among those who lined the route to honour the 23-year-old soldier from North Vancouver.
Gardner, a veteran of the Canadian Armed Forces, shared his deepest condolences for Goulding's family and said the young soldier "mattered to the country."
"It's so important that they can at least take that with them, that we all feel deeply, deeply affected," he said.
"I know that all of Canada is feeling heartbroken about what happened," Gardner said.
Pte. Aidan Goulding, from 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia’s Canadian Light Infantry, was one of four soldiers killed in the fire. (Submitted by Sonia Monk)
Goulding was among four soldiers killed in the blaze that overwhelmed a live-fire training exercise at Wainwright on Oct. 17.
The others killed were: Pte. Hayden Lykkemark, 19, of Langley, B.C.; Sgt. Morgan Wong, 26, of Edmonton; and Pte. Shaun Farrell, 23, from Prince Albert, Sask.
Farrell's funeral was held in his hometown on Wednesday, attended by Saskatchewan Premier Scott Moe and members of Farrell's unit.

items: Canada-wide support grows for CFB Wainwright victims as 50 investigators probe deadly fire
Sask. soldier killed in CFB Wainwright fire remembered as funny, passionate at military funeral

blocks.text: Fire Chief Jim Wishlove from Richmond Fire-Rescue said first responders had come from across Metro Vancouver to pay their respects to Goulding and the other soldiers who died, while showing support for their families.
"We're hurting with them today," he said.
"It brings it to light for us how incredibly dangerous all of these jobs are, and particularly the Armed Forces.
"These people are serving their communities, serving Canada."
Community gathers for funeral of Sask. soldier killed at CFB Wainwright

Brennan MacLachlan, a reservist with the Canadian Armed Forces and the emergency programs manager for the City of Richmond, said no words could assuage the grief the families of the soldiers who died are feeling.
"But we stand with them," he said, after the motorcade carrying Goulding's remains passed by.
"It's a weight that we all carry."

blocks.text: Politics·New
Alexander MacDonald was named the new president of the Canadian Space Agency late Wednesday evening.
Alexander MacDonald helped establish the 'Moon to Mars' strategy that includes the Artemis mission
Industry Minister Mélanie Joly made the announcement in Ottawa during a tribute event to the late Marc Garneau, the first Canadian to travel to space.

MacDonald served as NASA's first chief economist, according to a government news release. In that role, he helped establish the "Moon to Mars" strategy, which includes the recent Artemis II mission that saw Canadian Jeremy Hansen travel around the moon earlier this year.
"As incredible as this year has been, I am even more excited about what the future holds for Canadians in space," MacDonald told the Ottawa crowd at Thursday's event.
"Space has never been more important for the strength and future of Canada, and never before has the world looked to Canada more for global leadership in the space domain."

items: Canada can't launch rockets on its own. A handful of companies want to change that

blocks.text: MacDonald takes over from Campbell

MacDonald is taking over from outgoing president Lisa Campbell, who had been in the role since 2020. His appointment comes as Prime Minister Mark Carney's government looks to expand Canada's space capabilities.
Earlier this month, Joly also appointed Hansen as a special advisor to the government on developing a new space strategy.

The federal government listed space-based platforms for surveillance as a key priority in its new defence industrial strategy released in February. The Carney government is also looking to expand co-operation with European countries in space as part of the proposed partnership with the European Union.

Published November 5, 2026 9:34am
The Philippines on Thursday conducted its Fourth Quarter Nationwide Simultaneous Earthquake Drill (NSED) featuring a magnitude 8.5 earthquake and tsunami scenario.

The Office of Civil Defense (OCD) led the exercise in the designated main pilot area, Santa Ana, Cagayan, in collaboration with various government agencies, uniformed services, and local government units.

articles.title: [Good Business] Sari-sari stores: Kapwa at play amid economic crises
articles.summary: Sari-sari stores are far from a perfect model but it is a lifeboat that the country relies on amid rising oil prices and political instability

blocks.text: Your childhood was incomplete had you not been asked to buy a thing or two from your local sari-sari (small neighborhood convenience) store. Be it as simple as patis (fish sauce) or toyo (soy sauce) to complete today’s ulam (viand), or even a sachet of detergent to finish one’s laundry, these tried and tested local stores have been a staple in the lives of Filipinos.

My exposure to the business model has been quite in-depth, at least for the past couple months, as a budding category manager for an FMCG (Fast-Moving Consumer Goods). Not often is it pointed out that 1.3 million of these shopping points are scattered across the archipelago–withstanding the aggressive expansion of giant hypermarket chains and an ever-evolving retail trade landscape.

There’s a Pinoy adage that goes “Huwag i-smallin” or not to belittle something and I would care to argue that it applies to how we see these stores each day. From a consumer goods perspective, one cannot hope to grow their business in the Philippines if they do not crack the route-to-market (RTM) recipe for sari-sari stores. These local shops help provide proximitized availability of the goods we so-carefully craft inside boardrooms to be within arms reach of the shoppers.

Setting aside FMCG nomenclature, one cannot help but see how innately Filipino this system translates into trade. Every now and then–and just so my manager reads it as firm proof of my diligence–I would go around our village, even outside to nearby neighborhoods checking on how our products fair in different channels. This practice of trade visits is a staple within the category development and sales industry in general as it allows us to see the realities, keeping our strategizing grounded especially in dire times such as now. It goes without saying that realizations also came into play as I went on these occasional rounds.

“Isang tawid lang kasi.” (It’s just a short distance to the store.) I recall a casual conversation with a more senior shopper in our village as she justified her preference of buying from their sari-sari store. Just when I thought her story was finished, she came closer, clutching her Good Morning towel and whispered “Tsaka puwede kang umutang.” (Plus, you can buy on credit.) It all seems stereotypical but the simple truth one can derive from this testament is the importance of credit in this business model.

Palista, utang muna, (List it, buying on credit) or whatever term may be affixed to this extension of credit is undoubtedly a crucial advantage of sari-sari stores among other channels. What’s striking, at the very least, is how both shoppers and shop owners see that these local credit lines allow a “lifeline” of sorts.

For shop owners, the act of pautang (lending) is a necessity. “Ito na rin pakikisama namin. Kapag hindi ka nagpautang, hindi na sila babalik.” (This is how we get along with others. If you don’t let them buy on credit, they won’t return.) A rather profound statement that proves how extending credit is a unique value proposition for sari-sari store owners in retaining shopper loyalty. Nonetheless, one can also interpret that this crucial tactic is not merely an “always on promo” but a compassionate gesture. Bullseye on the mention of the word pakikisama (getting along) as this solidifies that, at the onset, entrepreneurial thinking and humanistic insights go hand-in-hand. At the very least, we can surmise that kapwa (shared humanity) is not undermined by kita (profit) but is actually driven by the former.

On the other side of the coin, we look at how shoppers rely on the palista (credit list) system. Now, more than ever, when “isang kahig, isang tuka” (hand to mouth existence) is not just a dramatic line for jesting but a harsh truth lived by the majority of Filipinos is the importance of surviving everyday. By allowing shoppers to accrue their payables, sari-sari stores provide an extension for hardworking Pinoys to make ends meet until the next payday.

Sure, boundaries are often set. More often than not do we hear horror stories of customers over-extending their credit yet the system of trust is undoubtedly integral to sustain this rather unique model. Pakikipagkapwa, as more formally referred to, banks heavily on the concept of seeing things in the perspective of others which conversely allows Filipinos to know their boundaries, albeit even in their sari-sari store transactions. Simply put, we know up to what extent we may lend a hand to our neighbors and we know our limits in accepting such help—hiya (shame) acting as a sort of internal moral compass.

Sari-sari stores are far from a perfect model but it is a lifeboat that the country relies on amid rising oil prices and political instability. Through each assortment offered in urban jungles to the most remote islands, essential goods are readily available while allowing tight-budgeted Filipinos an opportunity to survive an increasingly hard economy.

From time to time, we will see a “Bawal umutang” (No credit allowed) signage in all capital letters. Then again, an Aling Belen or Mang Tony would be amiable enough to have a handy list of their pautang (items on credit list)—allowing us to see good business in practice. It comes off as a two-way street if you ask me: retaining customers while also allowing a sense of ginhawa (relief) to an already struggling individual. Call it good karma, if you may, but this thinking perhaps actualizes the sustainability of the sari-sari store model.

Next time we pass by to get our fix of pancit canton or sitsirya (snack food), I openly welcome anyone to ask their sari-sari store owners how they are fairing these days. This gesture is not merely an intellectual exercise but a sort of pakikipagkapwa (solidarity)—allowing us to better understand their situation and support local businesses in a more sustainable way. – Rappler.com

Leon “Eo” Matawaran is a commercial development executive (category manager) from Nestle Philippines, Inc. handling NESTEA. Aside from being a category manager, he is a culture and inclusivity advocate that champions Filipino values in leadership—among other humanistic initiatives.

articles.title: Datacenters were on the ballot. US voters rejected them
articles.summary: Voters approved nearly every datacenter moratorium that was on the ballot, dozens in total in Tuesday’s elections

blocks.text: There were three big losers in Tuesday’s midterm elections in the US: Donald Trump, Elon Musk and datacenters.

Datacenters, the facilities full of semiconductor chips that power artificial intelligence and a host of other online products, were on the ballot in elections in at least 40 jurisdictions across 10 states. Voters responded with a strong rebuke of the giant buildings, which have has become a symbol of the tech industry and AI.

In Ohio alone, at least 14 municipalities passed bans or restrictions on datacenter development, including in Sunbury, where Amazon has proposed a $2m datacenter project. In Maine, eight municipalities passed temporary datacenter moratoriums. In Emporio, Kansas, where a 1,000-acre gigawatt-scale datacenter was recently proposed, a ban on high-impact datacenters was approved by voters.

Voters approved nearly every datacenter moratorium that was on the ballot, dozens in total, with one notable exception: Hardwood, North Dakota. The small city of a population of less than 1,000 people voted down a bill that would impose restrictions on datacenter development.

Where datacenters were not explicitly on the ballot, officials who have pushed back against their development were elected. In Texas, Democrat Gina Hinojosa, who secured a historical victory as governor on Tuesday night over her Republican opponent, has promised to impose moratoriums on their construction. She has pledged to implement greater restrictions on and community input into whether datacenters can be built. Towards the end of his tenure, Greg Abbott, her Republican opponent, had also tried to capitalize on anti-datacenter sentiment, demanding an end to electricity subsidies for them. He reversed his previous stance that had welcomed datacenters to the state.
Keisha Lance Bottoms, who became governor of Georgia, and Amy Acton, the newly elected governor of Ohio, have also pledged to implement moratoria on the construction of large datacenters.

Anti-datacenter sentiment has grown in the last few months has become a bipartisan issue. In May, Florida governor Ron DeSantis signed a bill imposing strict regulations on large-scale datacenters. Still, last night’s election solidified the overwhelming opposition to these centers of compute that have come to serve as a stand-in for the ultra wealthy and resource extraction by the AI industry.
“Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now,” Elon Musk, who poured over $400m into supporting conservative candidates, posted on X.
Analyst Dan Ives said the results of the midterms are a clear sign that the pace of datacenter buildout will start to slow down.
after newsletter promotion

“There is no way to sugarcoat that Democrats taking control especially over the Senate will create some major hurdles for AI and tech legislation in the Beltway over the next two years,” Ives said. Ives said he was particularly worried about Hinojosa who is a “known anti-datacenter politician”.
“The biggest worry of the night for tech investors and the AI trade was around the state of Texas where 25%-30% of data center gigawatts and capacity will come from,” he said.

articles.title: Filipino teens among least physically active globally — WHO study
articles.summary: Around 40% of Filipino adolescents reported no day with at least 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity in a week

blocks.text: November 5, 2026 | 9:26am
MANILA, Philippines — About two in five Filipino adolescents reported getting less than an hour of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity, falling behind their counterparts around the world.
The World Health Organization's latest survey foudn tha taround 40% of adolescents aged 11 to 17 in the Philippines reported having no "active day" in a week.
An active day was defined as one with at least 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity, such as brisk walking, cycling, playing sports or other activities that raise the heart rate.
The study, published in The Lancet Global Health, draws on hundreds of population-based surveys from 140 countries and territories, involving more than 3.2 million teens.

The Philippines was grouped with Namibia and Nepal, where around 40% of adolescents also reported no active days. By comparison, the global average was about 25%. This makes the Philippines' youth among the least active in the world.
Over the years, overall inactivity barely changed and even marginally declined in the Philippines, from 40.85% in 2010 to 40.32% in 2025.
Filipino girls are even less active than their male counterparts in the 2025 findings, with 42.7% reporting having no active day compared with 38% of boys.
The trend is similar globally. Only 11% of girls said they were active every day, compared with 17% of boys.
"For 15 years, the world has made almost no progress in getting young people moving, and girls are being left furthest behind," WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said.
PHILIPPINES | WORLD HEALTH ORGANIZATION DATA
4 in 10 Filipino adolescents report zero active days
Percentage of adolescents reporting no physically active days in the previous week, 2021–2025
Source: World Health Organization, physical activity data, Philippines, 2021–2025.
Global progress stalls
Worldwide, one in four adolescents aged 11 to 17 reported no active days in the previous week, according to estimates published in The Lancet Global Health.
That amounts to around 240 million young people.
The study drew on 389 population-based surveys from 140 countries and territories involving more than 3.2 million adolescents.
On average, adolescents reported being active for 2.7 days a week, while only 14% said they were active for at least 60 minutes on all seven days.
The WHO warned that physical inactivity is a major risk factor for heart disease, type 2 diabetes and some cancers.
"Helping young people develop active habits early in life is critical to protecting their health and reducing the global burden of these diseases," the agency said.
The study found little global progress over the past 15 years, with adolescent physical activity levels remaining virtually unchanged since 2010.
More than individual choice
The WHO said physical activity depends partly on the environments in which adolescents live, study and travel.

Access to safe public spaces, opportunities to walk or cycle, transportation systems, school environments, affordability and social norms can all affect how active young people are. Increasingly screen-centered lifestyles may also play a role.
"The answer is not to tell adolescents to try harder. It is to build schools, streets and communities where moving, playing and being active is safe, easy and normal," Tedros said.
The WHO called for stronger action across education, transport, urban planning, sports and health to make physical activity easier and safer for young people.
"Countries need policies that make physical activity an easy, safe and accessible part of everyday life," the agency said. — Camille Diola with Agence France Presse

articles.title: Beach weather in November? In Canada? These photos prove it
articles.summary: Parts of Ontario and Quebec have been experiencing record-setting temperatures this week, and people have been taking full advantage of it.

image.caption: A woman stands in the St. Lawrence River at Verdun Beach as temperatures soar in Montreal on Wednesday. (Christinne Muschi/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Canada·Photos
Parts of Ontario and Quebec have been experiencing record-setting temperatures this week, and people have been taking full advantage of it.
Parts of Ontario and Quebec have been basking in summer-like weather this week
Even at the best of times, it's hard to imagine swimming outdoors in November — no matter where you live in Canada. But 2026 is changing that conventional wisdom.
Parts of Quebec and Ontario have been experiencing potentially record-setting summer-like temperatures this week, with highs over 20 C.
Normal highs in major cities this time of year are around 10 C.
In Montreal on Wednesday, it was 22 C, but felt like 24 C. Good enough for a trip to the beach.
A woman enjoys the warm weather at Verdun Beach in Montreal on Wednesday. (Christinne Muschi/The Canadian Press)

According to the Weather Network, the weather anomaly is due to a strong, high-pressure ridge off the U.S. East Coast and a warm front associated with a Colorado low — a low-pressure area caused by the Rocky Mountains that tends to track northeastward. Those systems combined are pushing warmer air into parts of Canada.
Toronto has also been warmer than normal.
With a high around 21 C in Toronto Wednesday, some people took to a hammock to enjoy the sunshine. (Chris Young/The Canadian Press)
Wearing shorts in Toronto in November? Why not? This man took advantage of the warmth as he walked his dogs Tuesday. (Alex Lupul/CBC)
What’s behind the warm November weather in London?
El Niño effect
This year's strong El Niño is probably part of the story, too.
Bill Merryfield, a research scientist at Environment and Climate Change Canada, says El Niño usually affects Canada toward the end of the year, causing unusually mild fall and winter temperatures.

"This year's event is truly exceptional because this warming has already exceeded three degrees, which is well above that of any previous event and is expected to go even higher before the usual peak of El Niño in November or December," he said, referring to Pacific Ocean temperatures tied to the weather phenomenon.
Two people take a break on Parliament Hill during an unseasonably warm Nov. 4. (Dan Taekema/CBC)
It was a warm day under the fall foliage at Toronto's High Park. (Alex Lupul/CBC)
A cyclist in Toronto took advantage of the delayed start of cooler temps, too. (Alex Lupul/CBC)
People had the same idea in western Quebec, too.
With files from The Canadian Press

articles.title: Hubert Aiwanger, prominent German politician, found dead in Berlin hotel
articles.summary:
Police and prosecutors open investigation into death of the 55-year-old Bavarian state deputy leader

A prominent German politician was found dead in a Berlin hotel on Wednesday, police said,…

blocks.text: A prominent German politician was found dead in a Berlin hotel on Wednesday, police said, adding they had launched an investigation.
The cause of death of Hubert Aiwanger, 55, who was deputy leader of southern Bavaria state, was not immediately clear.
Police said in a statement he was “found dead in his hotel room” in the Berlin-Mitte district.
Police and prosecutors had opened a probe to “determine the specific cause and circumstances of death”, the statement said.

“The aim ⁠of the inquest is to establish the ​specific cause of death ‌and the ‌circumstances surrounding it, and to rule out any ‌possible third-party culpability,” police and prosecutors said in a statement. They gave no further details.

Aiwanger, head of the populist Free Voters party and also Bavarian economy minister, was in Berlin to attend the opening of an office for his party but missed the event as he was feeling unwell, the Bild daily reported.
His body was later discovered by police in the hotel, it said.
The Bavarian state premier, Markus Soeder, described Aiwanger’s death as an “absolute tragedy”.
“We are all deeply shocked. Our thoughts are now first and foremost with his family and his children,” he said.
Aiwanger’s party were junior partners in the regional Bavarian government led by Soeder’s Christian Social Union (CSU).

He had headed the Bavarian branch of the Free Voters since 2006. Under his leadership, the party made it into the state government for the first time in 2018, but never won enough seats to qualify for Germany’s federal parliament.
Aiwanger had faced national controversy in 2023 after reports emerged that he wrote an antisemitic pamphlet as a 17-year-old schoolboy, in which Auschwitz was described as an “entertainment quarter”.
He denied having written the pamphlet, though he has admitted to having had “one or a few copies” of it in his school bag. He apologised over the affair but refused to step down.
Aiwanger had two children and lived with his partner, German media reported.
With Agence France-Presse and Reuters

articles.title: Pete Hegseth may take fall for Republicans’ midterm losses, despite Trump support
articles.summary: JD Vance calls Iran war into question as Thomas Massie files eight articles of impeachment

blocks.text: Pete Hegseth is increasingly looking like he may take the fall for Republicans’ midterm losses, despite Donald Trump’s vocal support for his defense secretary, even calling him a champion of war.

The war in Iran, which voters and Trump have named as a key reason for Republicans’ midterm losses, “has been primarily a Department of War-led effort because you chose to take military action to resolve a foreign policy matter”, a former senior Pentagon official told CNN.

“If the president is serious about anyone taking responsibility for it, it’s Pete Hegseth,” one Republican close to the White House added in an interview with CNN. “Pete has been either dishonest or incorrect – neither of which are acceptable – about timelines, goals and objectives since the beginning.”
On Wednesday, JD Vance publicly questioned whether the Iran war was worth it and said it cost Republicans control of Congress.
Thomas Massie, a Republican congressman from Kentucky, has already filed eight impeachment accusations against Hegseth, and plans to soon force a House vote on the impeachment.
Trump has repeatedly defended Hegseth and, in speaking with reporters on Wednesday about whether he was considering replacing Hegseth, said: “No, I think ⁠he’s doing a very good job.”

Kingsley Wilson, the Pentagon press secretary, said: “The entire Department is unified behind the Secretary’s vision and will continue working to put our warfighters and America first,” in a statement to USA Today on Wednesday.

Trump has described Hegseth as a key proponent of the unpopular conflict, saying on 23 March: “Pete, I think you were the first one to speak up, and you said: ‘Let’s do it, because you can’t ⁠let them have a nuclear weapon.’”
Hegseth has been a polarizing figure in American politics and has made enemies even with his own Republican party.

Thom Tillis, the Republican US senator, told CBS News on Tuesday night that Hegseth had “a reckoning” coming and his strained relationship with lawmakers was undermining the Trump administration’s push for a $1.5tn defense spending package in Congress.

“I think after the election, we need to determine whether or not he’s the best person to bring those needs to Congress if he wants something done before the end of this Congress, which is only 60 days away,” Tillis said as the midterm results came in.

Democrats have promised to investigate Hegseth and his handling of the Pentagon, and aides say that could include everything from his handling of the Iran war to his purges of top military officers, including the chair of the joint chiefs of staff.
He could also face ‌scrutiny over his Ukraine policy and US military strikes on alleged drug-trafficking boats in Latin American waters, which some Democrats say could amount to war crimes.

Adam Smith, the Democratic representative who is expected to lead the House armed services committee next year, promised vigorous oversight on everything from the Iran war to what he called the erosion of the “apolitical foundation of the armed forces”.
